exposure: mode of delivery (vaginal delivery vs. caesarean section)
cohort: The study included women admitted to the labour ward with Pregnancy Induced Hypertension (PIH) who delivered babies weighing less than 2.5kg, through either vaginal delivery or caesarean section.
finding: Caesarean delivery offered no short-term survival advantage compared with vaginal delivery for low birth weight vertex-presenting fetuses in PIH patients.
mod_finding: There was no statistically significant difference in overall early neonatal outcome between vaginal delivery and caesarean section groups for low birth weight babies born to mothers with PIH, indicating no short-term survival advantage for caesarean delivery.
cross-section timing: Early neonatal period (first week after delivery)
